clock_time_reference: The Democracy Clock remained at 8:14 p.m. this week, with no net movement. That stillness reflected a balance between measurable executive consolidation and meaningful judicial resistance, not an absence of danger.

grand_total_points.note: Despite many trait shifts, the weekly net clock change was zero minutes because democratic harms and institutional resistance offset each other in the aggregate.

delta_summary.moral_floor: No net clock movement did not signal stability; it marked a week in which coercive power became more durable even as courts kept drawing enforceable limits.
delta_summary.net_interpretation: This was a week of structural entrenchment held in check, not reversed. Congress and the executive deepened existing lines of democratic erosion, while courts prevented those gains from moving the dial further.

traits_moved.note: Twenty tracked traits registered movement, showing broad-based pressure across institutions, information, immigration, and corruption patterns.

long_synopsis: Week 73 was defined by entrenchment rather than rupture. Congress passed and President Trump signed roughly $70 billion in added funding for ICE and CBP, giving immigration enforcement a longer budget horizon and fewer practical constraints just as detention abuses, hunger strikes, and aggressive multi-state enforcement became more visible. The administration also sharpened a hierarchy of belonging through refugee policy, benefit cuts, and threats against noncooperating jurisdictions. At the same time, Trump pressed against institutional referees, attacked Senate procedure, and advanced loyalty-centered nominations for justice and intelligence posts. Records fights deepened around the Epstein files, while official messaging and paid amplification further degraded the information sphere. Yet courts repeatedly blocked or narrowed executive overreach, from the anti-weaponization fund to immigration fees and institutional interference. The clock did not move because consolidation and resistance advanced together.
short_synopsis: Congress locked in major new immigration enforcement funding, the executive pressed against oversight and procedure, and the information sphere worsened. Courts still imposed meaningful checks, so the Democracy Clock held at 8:14 p.m. even as coercive power became more durable.
